title: Anchored audit checkpoint orchestrator and retention enforcer
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a resilient service that creates periodic, verifiable audit checkpoints for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes; deposits checkpoint bundles into customer-region WORM-backed storage; and exposes automated evidence exports for legal hold and compliance reporting.

Scope:
- Produce lightweight checkpoint artifacts (compact event list + metadata) every 5 minutes and on-demand for high-severity events.
- Each checkpoint must include incremental Merkle root, sequence number, timestamp, and KMS-signed attestations.
- Store checkpoints in region-scoped WORM object storage with immutable retention metadata and replication controls tied to customer residency policy.
- Provide evidence export API that bundles a signed sequence of checkpoints, integrity proofs (Merkle branch), and human-readable index for audits.
- Integrate with Console to show per-customer retention policy, last checkpoint time, and export history.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term archival analytics pipeline and cross-account multi-tenant index search (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Checkpoint generator produces signed artifacts every 5 minutes in the configured customer region.
2) Artifacts written to WORM-backed bucket show immutable retention metadata and cannot be overwritten or deleted before TTL expires.
3) Proof bundle API returns a zip containing checkpoints, Merkle proofs, and signature chain; bundle verifies against KMS public keys.
4) Console displays last checkpoint time and retention policy for the customer; clicking "View evidence" returns the signed bundle.
5) Load test demonstrates generation at 10k events/min across shard set without falling behind by more than 1 checkpoint interval.
implementation_notes:
- Checkpoint payload should avoid storing full event payloads; include deltas and pointers to encrypted event blobs to limit size.
- Use a Merkle tree over event IDs + sequence to support compact membership proofs for slice exports.
- Sign Merkle root with customer-scoped KMS key; fallback signing uses platform key with reason logged if customer key unavailable.
- Write to provider-specific immutable storage APIs (S3 Object Lock compliance mode for us-east, Azure Blob immutable policy in eu-west, and GCS retention pins) via an abstraction layer.
- Retention enforcement will be handled by the storage driver; add periodic audits that validate immutability controls and surface drift to Console.
- For private/VPC installs, offer a local-compatible driver that marks objects immutable using the appliance's storage controls and includes signed attestations in metadata.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Proof granularity: per-event proofs increase bundle size but improve selective verification; defaulting to per-checkpoint Merkle proofs reduces storage but requires reconstructing event membership when requested.

Retention enforcement vs legal requests: we must support legal-hold overrides without breaking WORM guarantees. Proposal: attach legal-hold metadata that prevents automatic TTL-driven deletion but still surfaces to compliance team for governance.
Signing model: prefer customer KMS key for non-repudiation, but some customers cannot provide keys in time. Accept fallback signed by platform key with audit annotation — need legal sign-off.
Cross-region notarization: do we replicate checkpoint to a secondary region for geo-redundancy and cross-proofing? This increases cost and complexity for some customers.
Performance: building Merkle trees at high write rates could be CPU intensive. Consider incremental tree updates and background compaction tasks.
